# Pre-migration sharing baselines

These synthetic stores and replies were captured at `8ddd83bc6396a77fa71e13509ac9c0910ef33e39`, schema 27. Open a private copy of each `.db`, not the original. Each database is a standalone SQLite `VACUUM INTO` copy; no sidecar or external source data is needed. Do not regenerate these files after changing the store or the handlers.

| Store | What wrote its history and local state |
| --- | --- |
| `legacy-zero` | Legacy `identity_log.enable` starting at base 0, with no imported agents. `finish_enable` records the operator `agent.cutover`, the shared canonical `root_key.backfill` and an empty enable payload. A legacy shared attempt creates an agent. `Switch::advance` writes `log.migrated`; `install_hub_snapshot` writes the two journal forms for multipart switch snapshots (a local audit row with no entry, then a shared row carrying the canonical image). |
| `legacy-supersede` | A restored copy of the log writer enables at nonzero base, writing the same backfill form and `identity_log.enable` with `supersedes_through`. Engram catch-up applies the peer member box and name, an ordinary project delta, and the two-part snapshot. Its switch consumes the exclusion proposal *as recorded by* `--without`, with the excluded box in the marker and snapshot. The test double supplies that proposal record so there is no Callosum dependency. |
| `legacy-catch-up` | An empty registry catches up through the initial snapshot, the superseding snapshot, the ordinary deltas, the multipart snapshot and the switch marker, then installs the hub image. The catch-up writer emits the initial `agent.import` and `agent.cutover`, a later import for the changed image, and `finish_join_at_head` emits its empty enable payload. Snapshot journal `entry` holds the merged replay image on the first row and an empty image on the next part; `payload_json.snapshot_part` retains each original body. |
| `native-enabling` | `begin_hub_enable` saved a native plan. The ID, canonical image and digest are intact, and the log base is null. |
| `native-installed` | Installs the saved native plan. The install writes `identity_log.enable` with `{}` and a completed `hub.snapshot`; the plan columns are cleared. Also holds an unresolved hub attempt with two sends, held epoch rows, a role generation high-water mark and a pending legacy entry with its reply continuation. |
| `disabled` | Local data and a cloud role observation, a local role from the legacy take writer, an enrollment-only role and a cached claim. |
| `switch-observer` | Joins a live in-process test harness backed by `nats-server`, from an empty registry. The Switch-era hub is built from `HubSnapshot`, with base 17, an excluded former box and surviving `engram:` holders and name. The store is captured just after snapshot install, before starting the tail and the residence watch. The paired observer already holds epoch 1, so it has no accepted signed KV bytes tying it to the original NATS process. The file keeps the old schema, a cloud role observation, an enrolled role, a cached claim and an unanswered legacy write with its reply continuation. |

The history files record both local (`here`, canonical entry and request payload) and remote (`log`, signed audit fields plus canonical entry) `member.set_box` and `member.set_name`. The switch marker has its original typed body and author in the journal; replay validates the shared bytes but has no derived-table effect. Backfill restores root keys; `agent.import` and the two kinds of snapshot restore earlier projections; `identity_log.enable` marks when replay starts treating project writes as shared. `agent.cutover` also records enrollment without changing the project or member projections.

`*.prefixes.json` lists every journal prefix ending immediately before a snapshot row, including the legacy backfill image and the intermediate hub audit row. All derived tables are dumped after replay, including empty tables. A store without a snapshot prefix has `[]`.

`*.default.jsonl` and `*.unselected.jsonl` are the served replies with no residence service, under normal test startup and forced zero hub membership respectively. `*.refresh.jsonl` uses an explicit selection in each direction. The status pairs preserve the RPC envelope and the actual CLI renderer's stdout. The clock is 700 and the status error state is clear. JSONL rows embed success bytes unchanged; typed handler refusals are represented as `error` objects.

`switch-observer.*.jsonl` records the existing member (holding the local role lease), the empty-registry joiner, its installed restart from a copy of `switch-observer.db`, and its readmission in episode 1 following removal. The reads wait for the residence watch and the identity-log cursor, and keep the handler and lease clocks fixed. The ordinary post-snapshot entry is applied once on the restarted observer, as on the other peers. The `engram:` agent's session residence is `unknown` even though its holder and epoch remain visible.
